svg.title: Self-consistent projection intuition diagram
svg.desc: A 2D point cloud projected onto a line. Vertical slices show that the conditional mean of each slice lands exactly on the projection line when self-consistency holds, and drifts off the line when it does not.
svg.text: Each slice's mean lands on the line
Slice means drift off the line → systematic bias
Self-consistency means: no systematic drift in any slice
Given a projection point Y on the line, average all original points that project there.
If E[X | Y] = Y, that average lands exactly back on Y — no bias in any direction.
This holds only when the projection axis aligns with an eigenvector of cov(X).
Otherwise, slice means systematically drift off the line → the approximation is biased.
